breaking_changes.BC_description: Most collection and control flow methods in the async library are now awaitable: if the final callback is omitted, these methods return a Promise instead of operating synchronously or expecting a callback. This changes the method signature and return value. Downstream code relying on synchronous return values, or that depends on passing callbacks to these methods, will need to adapt. Wrapping utility methods (like timeout, memoize, reflect, etc.) are not yet affected by this change and will not be awaitable at this time. Only collection and control flow methods listed in the commit messages are now awaitable when the callback is omitted.
Dropped out-of-the-box support for Node 4 and earlier, as well as many old browser versions, due to heavy use of ES2015 features. This breaks compatibility with these environments.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method: Upgrade your runtime to Node 6+ or a browser that supports ES2015 features.
breaking_changes.RequireInfo: List of minimum required runtime (Node versions & browser versions) is not fully specified. Explicit compatibility matrix is needed.

breaking_changes.BC_description:
The event-style properties 'drain', 'saturated', 'unsaturated', 'empty', and 'error' in the queue, priorityQueue, cargo, and cargoQueue classes have been changed from assignable callback properties to methods for registering callbacks. Instead of assigning a callback with 'q.drain = callback', you must now register it via method invocation, e.g., 'q.drain(callback)'. If these methods are called without a callback, they return a Promise that resolves on the next occurrence of the event, enabling use with 'await'.

This is a breaking change: existing code that used 'q.drain = callback', 'q.saturated = callback', etc., will no longer work. You must replace all event-like property assignments for: 'drain', 'saturated', 'unsaturated', 'empty', and 'error' in the affected classes with method invocation syntax.

For example,
Before:
    q.drain = function() { ... }
    q.saturated = function() { ... }
    q.empty = fn;
    q.error = fn;
    q.unsaturated = fn;
After:
    q.drain(function() { ... })
    q.saturated(function() { ... })
    q.empty(fn)
    q.error(fn)
    q.unsaturated(fn)
To handle the event with async syntax:
    await q.drain()
    await q.empty()

In asynchronous flow-control methods such as 'eachOfLimit' (and all similar collection-based methods), 'compose', 'seq', 'waterfall', 'auto', 'autoInject', 'whilst', 'until', and 'forever', calling a step callback with 'false' as the first argument (e.g., callback(false)) will now immediately cancel further iteration and prevent any pending or final callbacks from being called. This breaks prior behavior where such a call was either ignored or treated as a successful step, and the flow would continue or the final callback was always invoked. Code relying on the final callback being triggered—even in cases of cancellation via 'callback(false)'—will no longer work as before. Existing code patterns that expect the final callback to always run, or that rely on error propagation semantics consistent with prior Node.js convention (where 'false' was not interpreted specially), will be disrupted. See PR #1064 and associated references for discussion and rationale.

In v3.0.0, async.during and async.doDuring were removed and replaced by async.whilst, async.doWhilst, async.until and async.doUntil. These methods no longer accept synchronous test functions; the test must now be asynchronous (returning a Promise or invoking a callback). In async.doWhilst(iteratee, test, callback), the iteratee runs once, then the async test is invoked with the results of the iteratee to decide whether to continue. The final callback receives the results of the last iteratee call.

All queue and collection methods in the library now throw an error if the 'limit' or 'concurrency' parameter is set to a value less than 1. Previously, passing a value less than 1 may have been allowed or resulted in undefined behavior. The following methods are affected: queue (constructor), priorityQueue (constructor), cargo (constructor), cargoQueue (constructor), mapLimit, eachLimit, filterLimit, reduceLimit, concatLimit, eachOfLimit, forEachOfLimit, groupByLimit. This change ensures that a RangeError is thrown immediately when an invalid limit or concurrency is provided to any of these APIs.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method:
Update all uses of the 'limit' or 'concurrency' parameters in the affected methods to ensure they are set to values greater than or equal to 1. For example:
// Before:
async.mapLimit(arr, 0, iterator, cb)
async.eachLimit(arr, 0, iterator, cb)
async.groupByLimit(arr, 0, iterator, cb)
// After (must be >= 1):
async.mapLimit(arr, 1, iterator, cb)
async.eachLimit(arr, 1, iterator, cb)
async.groupByLimit(arr, 1, iterator, cb)

Passing a value less than 1 (such as 0 or negative numbers) will now throw a RangeError and must be avoided.

breaking_changes.BC_description: 'async.memoize' no longer caches error results. Previously, if the callback passed to 'async.memoize' produced an error (i.e., called back with a non-null 'err'), the error result was cached, and subsequent calls with the same arguments would receive the cached error. As of this change, error results are not cached—each call that results in an error will execute the underlying function again. This affects all uses of 'async.memoize' with asynchronous functions where errors may occur.

The methods async.applyEach and async.applyEachSeries have been changed. They now always return a function that accepts a single callback argument. If this callback is omitted, the returned function becomes awaitable via Promise. Crucially, the partial application feature previously available in applyEach—where additional arguments could be bound to the function—has been removed. Functions returned from applyEach and applyEachSeries no longer support partial argument application; only a callback or .then/await Promise is supported. The method signature and return value shape are changed: previous usage passing arguments for partial application will break. For example, before: async.applyEach(fns, arg1, arg2, cb); now: const fn = async.applyEach(fns); fn(cb) or await fn().

A ESM-flavored async.mjs module is included and described in the 'module' field of package.json, which changes how module loading occurs with modern bundlers. This could break setups where the CJS version was being forcibly used.
breaking_changes.Adaptation_method:
Update your import statements or bundler configuration to consume the correct ESM or CJS variant as appropriate for your environment.
Example:
import async from 'async'; // Modern ESM import
// or ensure require('async') for CJS environments
